items.title: Lester Santiago Interview, 1959-01-09
items.q: And Harold Dajon would teach both of us. Old numbers he would find out from the captain if anybody had anything to sing, and so forth. And we would call rehearsal on the ship.

ctx.x: From New Orleans to New York City. And while traveling on a ship, they decided that the band would have to play to entertain the passengers. And those people had their own music. So they presented me the music on one trip, and I told them I didn't know how to read. So they got someone from off the ship, a passenger, to play my part. So Harold told me, he said, well, Leslie said you're a fine piano player, but they're going to have to leave you go, he said, because you don't read. He said, I've been behind you to…
Yeah, I worked with Larry too.

items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: See Lester was always a better band man than him

ctx.x: One time I had the idea he was mostly just a solo pianist, you know like playing by himself. Was he good in a band?

He was pretty good in a band but I mean he was better solo pianist by himself. He was not a good band man like Lester. See Lester was always a better band man than him, you know. He was a good band man. But just like you said, playing by himself, they couldn't touch him. They couldn't touch him, they couldn't do nothing. And I told you about when the barbers used to stand him up on the boxes, you know so he could reach the key. He was a small kid down here.
Yeah, he was playing for the small.
